# Test fixtures

This data is entirely fictional and can be recreated locally.

## `vault/`

A small fictional Obsidian vault: two `type: project` cards, their
summaries and details, two `type: session` notes, a `type: journal` note,
concepts, and AI notes. Cases covered: an accent in a title, a card whose
`source_path` is `none (not created yet)`, a stale `verified_commit`, an
orphan note, invalid YAML, two broken links, an alias, a link with an anchor,
an embedded image, a link ignored inside a code block, a nested `.obsidian`
note that is ignored, and a file stored with LF line endings.

## `vault/.vantage/repos`

Maps the project names Atlas and Compass onto `repos/alpha` and `repos/beta`, with paths relative to the vault. `import` and `watch` read it, and a `-repos` flag replaces a name. The cards themselves still say `source_path: none (not created yet)` and `source_path: C:/Fixtures/Compass`. The directory is hidden, so it is not imported as a note.

## `repos/`

Two Git repositories generated by `scripts/fixtures/make-repos.go`. `go test ./...` creates them when they are missing. The generator
pins `commit.gpgsign`, `core.autocrlf`, `core.filemode`, and `core.precomposeunicode`
so Linux, macOS, and Windows produce the same commit hashes. It
produces deterministic histories with several languages, ISO timestamps with
+02:00, -05:00, and +05:30 offsets (including 23:30 UTC rolling into the next
local day), several authors, a rename detected by `git log -M` of an unchanged
file longer than 10 lines, a path with a space and an accent, a multi-line
message, a binary file, and a merge. The generated Git directories are ignored
by Git and are deleted then recreated on every run.
